hints: Integrate the acceleration function $a = 0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2}$ with respect to $t$ to find the velocity function $v(t)$.
Since the particle starts from rest at $t = 0$, the constant of integration is zero: $c = 0$.
Instantaneous rest occurs when $v(t) = 0$. Factor out $t^{3/2}$ or divide by $0.1t^{3/2}$ for $t > 0$ to reach an equation of the form $t^{5/2} = k$.
Solve for $t$, then substitute this value into the acceleration function $a(t)$ to show that $a = 16\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Integrate acceleration $a = 0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2}$ with respect to time to find velocity $v$:
$$v = \int (0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2})\,dt = \frac{0.4}{4}t^4 - \frac{4.8}{3/2}t^{3/2} + c = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2} + c$$

Apply the initial condition: the particle starts from rest at $t = 0$, so $v(0) = 0 \implies c = 0$:
$$v = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2}$$

Set $v = 0$ to find when the particle comes to instantaneous rest in subsequent motion ($t > 0$):
$$0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2} = 0$$
$$0.1t^{3/2}(t^{5/2} - 32) = 0$$

Substitute $t = 4\text{ s}$ into the acceleration function:
$$a(4) = 0.4(4)^3 - 4.8(4)^{1/2} = 0.4(64) - 4.8(2) = 25.6 - 9.6 = 16\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that velocity is the indefinite integral of acceleration with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$
Substitute the given acceleration function $a(t) = 0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2}$:
$$v(t) = \int (0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2})\,dt$$
Integrate term by term using the power rule $\int t^n\,dt = \frac{t^{n+1}}{n+1}$:
$$v(t) = 0.4\left(\frac{t^4}{4}\right) - 4.8\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) + c$$
$$v(t) = 0.1t^4 - 4.8 \times \frac{2}{3}t^{3/2} + c = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2} + c$$

Use the initial condition that the particle starts from rest at $t = 0$ ($v = 0$ when $t = 0$):
$$0 = 0.1(0)^4 - 3.2(0)^{3/2} + c \implies c = 0$$
Thus the velocity at time $t$ is:
$$v(t) = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2}$$

Find when the particle comes to instantaneous rest by setting $v(t) = 0$:
$$0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2} = 0$$
Factor out $0.1t^{3/2}$:
$$0.1t^{3/2}(t^{4 - 3/2} - 32) = 0$$
$$0.1t^{3/2}(t^{5/2} - 32) = 0$$
For the subsequent motion, $t > 0$, so $0.1t^{3/2} \ne 0$:
$$t^{5/2} = 32$$

Solve for $t$ by raising both sides to the power $\frac{2}{5}$:
$$t = 32^{2/5} = (2^5)^{2/5} = 2^2 = 4\text{ s}$$

Evaluate the acceleration at this instant $t = 4\text{ s}$ using $a(t) = 0.4t^3 - 4.8t^{1/2}$:
$$a(4) = 0.4(4^3) - 4.8(4^{1/2})$$
$$a(4) = 0.4(64) - 4.8(2)$$
$$a(4) = 25.6 - 9.6 = 16\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the acceleration when the particle comes to instantaneous rest is $16\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: Displacement $s(t)$ is obtained by integrating the velocity function $v(t) = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2}$ with respect to $t$.
Since the particle starts at the origin $O$ at $t = 0$, evaluate the definite integral $\int_0^5 (0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2})\,dt$.
Compute the antiderivative $\left[0.02t^5 - 1.28t^{5/2}\right]_0^5$ and evaluate at $t = 5$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Integrate the velocity function $v(t) = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2}$ to find the displacement $s$ from $O$:
$$s = \int_0^5 (0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2})\,dt = \left[ \frac{0.1}{5}t^5 - \frac{3.2}{5/2}t^{5/2} \right]_0^5 = \left[ 0.02t^5 - 1.28t^{5/2} \right]_0^5$$

Round to three significant figures:
$$s = -9.05\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that displacement from a fixed origin $O$ is given by the integral of velocity with respect to time:
$$s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt$$
Substitute $v(t) = 0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2}$:
$$s(t) = \int (0.1t^4 - 3.2t^{3/2})\,dt$$
Integrate term by term:
$$s(t) = 0.1\left(\frac{t^5}{5}\right) - 3.2\left(\frac{t^{5/2}}{5/2}\right) + d$$
$$s(t) = 0.02t^5 - 3.2 \times \frac{2}{5}t^{5/2} + d = 0.02t^5 - 1.28t^{5/2} + d$$

Since the particle starts at the origin $O$ at $t = 0$, $s(0) = 0$, which gives $d = 0$:
$$s(t) = 0.02t^5 - 1.28t^{5/2}$$

Substitute $t = 5$ into the displacement formula:
$$s(5) = 0.02(5^5) - 1.28(5^{5/2})$$
Calculate each power:
$$5^5 = 3125$$
$$5^{5/2} = 5^2 \times \sqrt{5} = 25\sqrt{5} \approx 25 \times 2.236068 = 55.901699$$
Perform the arithmetic multiplications:
$$0.02 \times 3125 = 62.5$$
$$1.28 \times 55.901699 = 71.554175$$

Subtract the values to find the displacement:
$$s(5) = 62.5 - 71.554175 = -9.054175\text{ m} \approx -9.05\text{ m}$$
Thus the displacement of the particle from $O$ at $t = 5\text{ s}$ is $-9.05\text{ m}$.
